title: Array: swap two cells by dragging one onto the other
description: The core sorting move. With an array selected, drag a cell's value onto another cell to swap them (one undo step); optionally a brief swap animation. Marks travel with values.
acceptance_criteria: Drag cell i onto cell j swaps values (both directions, vertical arrays too); Esc cancels; undo; e2e.
close_reason: Per-cell handles; drag onto another cell swaps values + marks (one undo, Esc cancels), ghost + dashed target while dragging, CSS arc animation on swap. Vertical arrays too. e2e swap.e2e.ts.

title: Mark elements with highlight colours (compare, visited, pivot, sorted)
description: Per-element marks stored on the shape (key -> colour), applied live: hover an element and press 1-4 to toggle a colour (0 clears), or pick from a small palette. Works for array cells, list/tree/graph nodes and edges. Survives edits and re-layout; included in export; one undo per change.
acceptance_criteria: Mark array cells and list nodes in 4 colours via keys and the palette; marks follow nodes through insert/remove/drag; export shows them; e2e.
close_reason: Marks on any element: keys 1-4/0 on the element under the pointer (tldraw numbered toolbar shortcuts disabled), Mark submenu in the context menu, stored per shape (array/list/tree migrations), rendered on canvas and export, pruned on removal, swapped with values. Unit + e2e (marks.e2e.ts, migration).

title: Teaching moves for every structure: marks and named pointers
description: Live moves that apply to arrays, lists, trees, heaps and graphs alike, built once in the shared layers (cells / node-link base) so each structure gets them for free.

title: Distinct random values by default, plus a 'repeats allowed' fill mode
description: Random fills in 0..99 repeat often (about 37% chance of a duplicate in 10 values). BSTs need distinct keys and most textbook examples use distinct values. Make random (and letters, up to 26) draw without replacement, including when growing and inserting (skip values already present, typed or not); keep duplicates available as a new 'repeats' fill mode.
close_reason: random/letters draw without replacement (sorted modes strictly monotone) until the pool runs out; extend/insert skip present values; new 'repeats' fill mode keeps duplicates. 8 new unit tests.

title: Hover-revealed node and edge controls
description: A selected list shows ~20 widgets (drag handles, x, +, grips); trees and graphs would be unreadable. Show a node's x only while the pointer is over (or near) that node, and an edge's + only near that edge; grips stay visible. Touch (coarse pointer) shows everything, since there is no hover.
acceptance_criteria: Hover a node -> its x appears; move to the x and click it; + appears near the hovered arrow; nothing per-node shows otherwise; coarse pointer shows all; e2e updated.
close_reason: Node x / edge + appear only near the pointer (hover.ts, 16px reach; grips always shown); coarse pointers show all. Driver 'hover' command + e2e hoverNode helper; list-edit e2e updated and extended.

title: Grow handle: drag to add or remove elements after drawing
description: After an array or list is drawn, select it and drag a '+' grip past its end to add elements (one per cell / node step) or drag back to remove them. Existing (typed) values are kept; new ones follow the shape's fill mode (random continues the seeded stream, ascending/descending continue the run). One undo per drag, Esc cancels. Built on a tldraw 'create' handle (drawn only on hover) plus our own grip glyph, so later structures can reuse it.
acceptance_criteria: Array (both axes) and list (all four directions) grow and shrink via the grip; head stays put on the page for left/up lists; typed values survive; undo/Esc work; unit + e2e tests.
close_reason: Grow grip for arrays (both axes) and lists (4 directions): create-type handle + '+' glyph past the end; grownCount/extendValues pure + unit tests (59 total); e2e grow.e2e.ts (5 tests, x4 stable) incl. typed values kept, seeded continuation, head fixed for left lists, Esc, undo.

title: Node-link render kit: nodes, edges, arrowheads, labels
description: Theme-aware SVG primitives shared by component() and toSvg(): circle and box nodes, straight edges clipped to node boundaries, arrowheads, curved antiparallel edges (u->v and v->u), self-loops, edge labels (weights), null/ground marker, pointer-box arrows for list nodes. Geometry helpers are pure and unit-tested.
acceptance_criteria: Used by at least the list shape; edge clipping/curving covered by vitest; looks right in light and dark export.
close_reason: src/nodelink/geometry.ts + SceneSvg.tsx: circle/box/list nodes, clipped straight edges, curved antiparallel twins, self-loops, arrowheads, edge labels, null/label annotations; pointer arrows take the shortest path. 16 vitest; list rendered in app; circles/curves/loops/labels checked visually via a rendered sample scene (light + dark).

title: Decide node-link representation: one model-driven shape vs tldraw node shapes + bound arrows
description: Lists/trees/graphs could be (a) ONE custom shape per structure whose props hold the model (nodes, edges, per-node position overrides) and render everything in SVG, or (b) separate node shapes joined by tldraw arrows with bindings. This choice shapes every later wave.
design: DECIDED (2026-10-02): option (a), one model-driven shape per structure. Implemented as src/nodelink: subclasses of NodeLinkShapeUtil turn props into a Scene (pure), the base renders (SceneSvg, shared with export), edits values (sceneCells -> CellShapeUtil) and drags nodes via tldraw vertex handles placed on each node's bottom edge (centre handles covered the values). Drag offsets are stored per node (dx/dy) on top of the automatic layout; 'Re-layout' (context menu) clears them. Spike = the singly linked list (dds-55z.8), which became the real first consumer. Open UX question: dragging requires selecting the structure then grabbing the handle; revisit if teachers expect to grab the node body.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in design notes; a throwaway spike renders a 3-node list and drags one node, confirming the chosen approach in tldraw 5.5.
close_reason: Decided: one model-driven shape per structure; proven by the linked list (render, edit, drag, export, undo).

title: Wave 2: node-link foundations
description: Shared pieces every node-and-pointer structure (lists, trees, heaps, graphs) needs before its own tool: a representation decision, an SVG render kit for nodes and edges, node editing via the cell layer, node dragging, structure options in the style panel, seeded generation, and browser e2e tests.
close_reason: Wave 2 complete: node-link kit, seeded fills, node editing/dragging, style-panel options, e2e harness.

title: Array sketch tool: drag to grow cells with random integers
description: Custom 'array' shape + tool. Press and drag: a new cell appears every cellSize page pixels along the dominant drag axis (right/left/down/up), each filled with a random int. Dragging back shrinks the array (values are kept stable). One undo step per array; Esc cancels. Indices shown under/next to cells. Uses tldraw color style. SVG rendering so export works.
acceptance_criteria: Toolbar button + shortcut (A). Drag right/left/up/down produces a correctly oriented array; release selects it; undo removes it in one step; export to SVG/PNG includes cells, values and indices.
close_reason: Array shape + tool done: drag grows cells every cell-width in any of 4 directions, random ints 0-99, stable values on shrink/regrow, indices, colour/size/font styles, Esc cancel, single-step undo, SVG export. Verified with 13 unit tests and a headless-Chrome drive.

title: Scaffold Vite + React + TS app with tldraw
description: Vite React-TS project, tldraw dependency, full-screen <Tldraw> with persistenceKey, typecheck/build/test scripts, vitest.
acceptance_criteria: npm run dev shows a tldraw canvas; npm run build and npm test pass.
close_reason: Vite 8 + React 19 + TS 7 + tldraw 5.5 scaffold; dev/build/typecheck/test scripts; vitest passing.

title: drawds v1: sketchable data structures on tldraw
description: Teacher-facing whiteboard built on the tldraw SDK (https://tldraw.dev). Each data structure (array, matrix, linked list, stack/queue, tree, graph, map) is a custom tldraw shape plus a gesture-driven tool, so a teacher can sketch a structure in one stroke and get it pre-filled (empty, random, sorted, ...) and editable. Shared pieces: data/fill generators, theme-aware SVG rendering (so export to PNG/SVG for slides works), and UI overrides for the toolbar.
notes: Planning lens (from user testing of lists): for every structure, list the moves a teacher invokes live (insert, delete, extend, swap, mark, point, rotate...) and make them first-class beads in the wave, not afterthoughts. Creation gestures alone are not enough.

title: UI menus render in the browser's serif default at 12px
description: tldraw's UI inherits the page font and drawds never set one, so menus, the style panel and dialogs used Times at 12px (reported by the user 2026-10-03). Set a system sans-serif on .tl-container and 13px on menu items, tooltips, dialogs and the style panel (drawds.css).
close_reason: drawds.css: system sans-serif on .tl-container, 13px for tldraw buttons/labels, tooltips, toasts, dialogs and the style panel picker; kbd hints 12px.

title: Array playback: operations, frames and the play bar on arrays
description: Arrays are not NodeLinkShapeUtil, so playback (frame props, highlights, swaps, frame pointers), the play bar placement (playbackLayout) and context-menu operations (nodeOperations) only reached node-link shapes. Lift nodeOperations / playbackLayout to CellShapeUtil; ArraySvg draws a frame's values, flash, swap arcs, one-way moves, dimmed cells and frame pointers. New frame fields: dim (keys greyed out, replacing earlier ones, e.g. binary search's discarded half) and counts (comparisons / swaps, shown in the play bar). moves: a value copied from one element to another slides in (array shifting).
design: CellShapeUtil gains optional nodeOperations(shape, key) and playbackLayout(shape, strips); overrides.tsx NodeOperationsMenu and PlaybackOverlay test for CellShapeUtil. Frame.dim: string[] (replacing); Frame.counts: Record<string, number> (replacing); Frame.moves: [from, to][] (to's value slides in from from). Frame pointers that overflow the array's box during playback are accepted (as list frames do); see dds-55z.30.
close_reason: CellShapeUtil hosts nodeOperations/shapeOperations/playbackLayout and the operation prompt; arrays draw frames (values, marks, flash, dim, swap/move slides); step pointers drawn in the play overlay; play bar shows counts. Unit + e2e tests.

title: Simple sorts step by step: insertion, selection, bubble
description: Right-click the array: Sort step by step > Insertion / Selection / Bubble. i and j pointers, the pair being compared orange, swaps as the existing arcs, the sorted region green growing; narration per comparison and swap; counters for comparisons and swaps (a strip or the caption) so classes can compare the algorithms.
close_reason: Insertion (swap-based), selection, bubble (early exit) sorts step by step: i/j/min pointers, orange compared pair, swap arcs, green settled region, comparisons/swaps counts in the play bar. Sort step by step submenu.

title: Binary search with lo / mid / hi
description: On a sorted array (offer Sort first if it isn't): lo = 0, hi = n - 1; mid = (lo + hi) / 2, compare, lo = mid + 1 or hi = mid - 1, the discarded half greyed; found (green) or lo > hi (not found, the pointers crossed). Search for a cell's value or a typed one (operation prompt). Pointers slide; each step narrated as code.
close_reason: Binary search (lo/mid/hi, discarded half faded, unsorted warning step lighting the first out-of-order pair, crossing pointers incl. -1/n) plus linear search for contrast; comparisons counter. Context menu Search submenu, value prompt.

title: Array algorithms step by step (umbrella)
description: Arrays were the first structure but have had no step-through work, and sorting/searching is the most-taught step-through material. Everything needed exists: named pointers (i, j, lo, mid, hi) that slide, swap arcs, marks, the play bar (opens paused, narration, strips). Children: binary search, simple sorts, partition. Later: merge sort (needs auxiliary arrays), counting sort.

title: List reverse: prev, curr, next and the arrows flipping
description: Right-click the list: Reverse: prev = null, curr = head; next = curr.next, curr.next = prev (the arrow flips, curving back), prev = curr, curr = next; finally head = prev. The reversed list keeps its place on the page (drawn right to left).
close_reason: Closed

title: List delete: prev/curr walk, then prev.next = curr.next
description: Right-click a node: Delete <value>: prev and curr walk from the head, prev.next = curr.next (the arrow goes round the node), the node drops out, the list closes up; deleting the head is head = head.next.
close_reason: Closed

title: List find: curr walks from the head
description: Right-click a node: Find <value> (from the head), or Find a value... (a prompt, so missing values can be searched for): curr = head, compare, curr = curr.next; found (green) or curr == null.
close_reason: Closed

title: List insert after a node: new node, then the two pointer assignments
description: Right-click a node: Insert after <value>: node = new Node(v) appears below the gap, node.next = curr.next, curr.next = node (narrated: in this order, or the rest of the list is lost), then the list straightens; at the head too (node.next = head; head = node).
close_reason: Closed

title: Frames draw their own scene and pointers
description: Playback frames can carry a whole scene (a node not yet linked, an arrow re-pointed or curving back, a null marker) and their own pointers (curr, prev, next) that slide between steps; edges can bend; drawn at the shape's committed offset.
close_reason: Closed

title: Operations open paused; autoplay is a toggle
description: Requested 2026-10-03: the teacher sets the pace, so operations open ready on step 1 and wait for Right / Space / the bar; the bar's toggle turns on autoplay (remembered per browser). Playing is slower too (650 ms a step).
close_reason: Closed

title: Traversal frames: visit numbers, output, call stack or queue, recursion path
description: Pure generator over a binary tree. Current node red, nodes waiting on the call stack orange, visited blue and numbered; edges from the start to the current node lit while the recursion is down there; null children flash as base cases when nulls are shown. Strips (several at once): the output so far, and the call stack (pre/in/post) or queue (level). Narration per step ('Back at 42: visit it (3), then its right subtree').
acceptance_criteria: vitest: visit orders match reference recursive traversals; final state all visited blue and numbered, stack empty.
close_reason: Closed

title: Traverse from any node: pre-, in-, post- and level-order (trees and heaps)
description: Right-click a tree or heap node: Traverse from <value> > Pre-order / In-order / Post-order / Level-order (a submenu for node operations). Heaps highlight both views; level order lines up with the array.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: in-order on a BST outputs the keys sorted; level order on a heap outputs the array; Shift+Enter keeps the visited nodes as marks.
close_reason: Closed

title: Play bar stays up after an operation: review, replay, then dismiss
description: Reported 2026-10-02: the bar appears and disappears too quickly to use. After an operation finishes (result committed, one undo step) the bar stays on its last step: step back and forth through it, replay it, then dismiss (Done / Enter / Esc; Shift keeps the highlights as marks). Selecting something else or editing the shape dismisses it too. The bar and the queue/stack strip move to a screen overlay so they never leave ghosts (dds-55z.29).
close_reason: Closed

title: Pointers on every structure: placement, export, pruning, migrations
description: Arrays (above cells; right of a vertical array), lists (below nodes, clear of head), trees, heaps and graphs (above nodes). Several pointers on one element share a label ('lo, mid'). Included in the shape's bounds so exports keep them; pointers on removed elements go with them; a props migration for every shape.
acceptance_criteria: Migration unit tests per shape + e2e load of an old snapshot; export screenshot shows pointers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add, rename and remove pointers
description: Right-click an element: Pointer > the structure's usual names (arrays i, j, k, lo, mid, hi; lists curr, prev, next; trees root, curr, parent; heaps i, parent, child; graphs s, t, u, v), or Custom name. A name already on the shape moves there. Double-click a pointer to rename it; x or Delete removes it.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: add from the menu, custom name, rename, remove; one undo each.
close_reason: Closed

title: Move pointers: drag, or click and step with the arrow keys
description: Drag a pointer onto another element. Click a pointer to pick it up (ringed), then Left/Right (Up/Down for vertical arrays and trees) step it along its structure: array index +-1 including one past either end, list next/previous including null, tree children/parent, graph neighbour in that direction. The move animates.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: drag to another element; arrows step it, i walks to n, curr walks to null.
close_reason: Closed

title: Frames light edges, number nodes and show a queue/stack
description: Playback frames gain edge highlights (keyed edge:<id>, like edge marks), small badges on nodes (discovery order), highlights that can be cleared again, and a strip under the structure showing a queue or stack as boxes.
close_reason: Closed

title: BFS and DFS frames with narration
description: Pure, unit-tested generators. Neighbours in label order, out-edges when directed. BFS: dequeue (current red), examine each edge, newly discovered nodes orange with a green tree edge, done nodes blue, queue strip. DFS (recursive): go deeper along unvisited edges, back up when done, the recursion stack as the strip. Discovery numbers as badges; unreachable nodes stay plain.
acceptance_criteria: vitest: BFS order and tree edges match a reference; DFS order matches recursive DFS; e2e: run BFS from a node, step through, Shift+Enter keeps the tree as marks.
close_reason: Closed

title: Start an operation from a node (context menu)
description: Right-click a node: the structure offers operations starting there (graphs: breadth-first / depth-first search from it). A generic per-node operations hook on the node-link base, for later tree traversals and list finds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Step-by-step mode: operations start paused
description: A toggle in the play bar: when on, every operation opens paused on its first step and waits for Right/Space. Remembered per browser (a per-viewer convenience).
acceptance_criteria: e2e: with the toggle on, an operation waits on step 1 until stepped.
close_reason: Closed

title: Narration: one line per step
description: Each frame can carry a caption shown in the play bar ('50 > 42: go right', 'Swap 7 with its parent 12'). Captions for the existing BST insert/delete and heap insert/remove.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: the caption changes with the step.
close_reason: Closed

title: Play bar: pause, step back/forward, finish, cancel (and keys)
description: While an operation is open a small bar sits under the structure: back, play/pause, forward, step counter, cancel. Keys while it is open: Space play/pause, Left/Right step, Enter finish (Shift+Enter keeps the highlights as marks), Esc cancel. Stepping back replays the earlier state (values swap back). Stepping past the last frame commits.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: pause mid-operation, step back and forward, Esc leaves the shape unchanged, Enter commits one undo step.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mark edges as well as nodes (paths, spanning trees, cuts)
description: Point at an edge and press 1-4 (or use the context menu) to colour it, 0 to clear: the edge is drawn thicker in the mark colour, arrowhead included. Shared node-link layer (CellShapeUtil.markKeyAt, edge marks keyed edge:<id> like edge cells), enabled for graphs first; lists and trees need edge-mark pruning on structural edits before they opt in.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: marking an edge stores edge:<id>; removing the edge drops the mark; export draws it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Delete a node (and its edges) or a single edge
description: x on the hovered node removes it with its incident edges; x on the hovered edge removes just that edge (new removeEdge hook in the node-link base; edge buttons hide while a node is hovered so they don't crowd it). Marks on removed elements go with them.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: remove an edge, remove a node with its edges, marks pruned, one undo each.
close_reason: Closed

title: Connect grip: drag from a node to another node (edge) or to empty space (new connected node)
description: The teacher's most common graph move: 'connect B to E', 'add F next to B'. A small + grip on the hovered node's rim; dragging it shows a dashed preview edge (with arrowhead when directed), the target node ringed or a ghost node at the pointer. Drop on a node: new edge (no duplicates; weighted graphs open the new weight for typing). Drop in empty space: new node with the next label plus the edge, opened for editing. Drop back on the source: nothing. Esc cancels.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: connect two nodes, connect to empty space (node + edge), duplicate is a no-op, one undo each.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add a lone node: drag the graph's + grip to place it
description: For disconnected graphs and components: a + grip off the graph's lower right, like the grow grips of arrays and lists; drag it and a new node follows the pointer, dropped where released and opened for editing. Double-clicking empty canvas stays tldraw's 'add text', so annotations still work next to a graph.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: dragging the grip adds an unconnected node at the drop point; one undo.
close_reason: Closed

title: Heap: insert and extract live, with the sift path highlighted
description: Insert a value (append + sift-up) and extract the root (move last to root + sift-down) as instant actions on the selected heap, highlighting the nodes that moved; the array view updates in step. The step-by-step version is wave 7.
close_reason: Heap insert (append + sift-up) and remove/extract (last into the gap + sift down/up) play as chains of swap arcs in tree and array; playback engine (frames then one-step commit) in src/nodelink/playback.ts. e2e heap.e2e.ts.

title: BST: insert and delete a key live, with the search path highlighted
description: Type a key into a small box on the selected BST: it is inserted where it belongs and the comparison path is highlighted (marks). Delete via x handles all three cases (leaf, one child, two children via successor). Instant here; the step-by-step version is wave 7.
close_reason: Insert-a-key prompt animates the comparison path then the new node; x deletes with leaf / one child / successor cases; duplicates found not inserted; highlights fade, Shift keeps them as marks; one undo. e2e bst.e2e.ts.

title: Tree: show or hide null children
description: Toggle (style panel option) that draws null children as small null markers under leaves and one-child nodes, for teaching recursion base cases and pointer structure.
close_reason: drawds:nulls style prop + style panel toggle; null markers in every empty slot, laid out as phantom leaves. e2e.

title: Array: insert or delete at an index, shifting the rest
description: Reuse the list controls: an x on the hovered cell deletes it and shifts later cells left; a + between cells inserts there and shifts right (new value per fill mode, opened for editing). Shows the cost of shifting, contrasting with linked lists.
notes: 2026-10-03: step-by-step insert at index / delete a[k] done (context menu 'Insert / delete step by step': copies narrated a[i] = a[i+1], moves counter, values slide). Left: the hover x / + controls for quick instant edits.
close_reason: Step by step (context menu) plus quick hover controls: x on the hovered cell's corner deletes it, + on the nearest boundary (lower end) inserts a fill-mode value and opens it for typing; later values slide straight over; marks travel; one undo step each; touch shows all buttons.

title: Named pointers attached to elements (i, j, lo, hi, mid, curr, prev, root)
description: Teacher moves: put i / j / lo / mid / hi / curr / prev / root / u on an element to talk about a loop or a search; move it a step (i++) or drag it elsewhere; let it walk off the end (i == n, curr == null); rename or remove it. Pointers live in each shape's props (persisted), drawn as a label with a short arrow, and move smoothly. Children: add/rename/remove, move by drag and keys, every structure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Insert a node in the middle of a list
description: Head/tail insertion (grips) and removal (x per node) exist. Add insertion between two nodes: e.g. a small + on each next-arrow while the list is selected (click to insert after that node), and/or drag a node handle onto an arrow. New value follows the fill mode; one undo step; downstream nodes re-flow.
close_reason: + button mid-way along each next pointer (incl. tail->null) inserts after its node; value via insertValue (between neighbours for sorted fills); new node opens for editing via CellShapeUtil.editCell; one undo for the insert, one for the typed value. Generic insertOnEdge/canInsertOnEdge hook in NodeLinkShapeUtil (reusable for trees/graphs). 77 unit, 22 e2e (stable x2-3).

title: run-drawds skill: headless driver for launching and driving the app
description: Project skill at .claude/skills/run-drawds/ with driver.mjs (playwright-core + installed Chrome, stdin command language, auto-starts Vite) so agents can sketch, edit, screenshot and export without rediscovering the setup.
close_reason: SKILL.md + driver.mjs written; every code block re-run verbatim (setup, two driver scripts, human path, tests).

title: Wave 7: algorithms in motion (step-through operations)
description: Walk through operations step by step on the sketched structures: highlights, pointer movement and a one-line narration per step, forwards and backwards.

title: Graph structural edits: connect, add, delete (umbrella)
description: Live structural moves on a selected graph, one undo step each, using the hover-revealed controls of the node-link base. Split into children: connect grip, lone node grip, delete node / edge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Graph options: directed/undirected, weighted/unweighted, letters/numbers
description: Style-panel pickers, used before sketching and live on a selected graph. Directed shows arrowheads (each edge keeps its stored direction); back to undirected merges u->v / v->u twins into one edge. Weighted shows each edge's weight (always stored, so toggling is lossless). Labels relabel nodes A, B, C... or 0, 1, 2... in node order (0-based numbers suit dist[v]/visited[v] arrays).
acceptance_criteria: Pickers show with the graph tool or a graph selected; switching a selected graph applies at once as one undo step; e2e covers each.
close_reason: Closed

title: Graph model + random generators
description: Pure, seeded generator for the sketch gesture: given node positions in drag order, node k connects to its nearest earlier node (so the graph is always connected) and, with some probability, to one or two more earlier nodes within reach, skipping edges that would cross an existing edge, pass through a node or leave a too-narrow angle (planar-ish, not a hairball). Random edge orientation and weights 1-9 per seed. Node k's edges depend only on the seed and nodes 0..k, so the graph is stable while the drag grows it.
acceptance_criteria: vitest: connected, deterministic per seed, growth-stable (a longer sketch extends a shorter one), no crossing generated edges, weights in 1..9.
close_reason: Closed

title: Graph extras (Wave 6 core done)
description: Wave 6 core done 2026-10-02: sketch tool, connect / add / delete, directed / weighted / labels, edge marks, BFS / DFS. Open children are optional extras: layouts, adjacency views, generation options (DAG, density), reverse / re-wire edges, neighbour hover, extend a sketch.

title: Heap <-> array view (index mapping 2i+1 / 2i+2)
description: Show a heap's backing array under it, reusing the array rendering. Hover a node to highlight its index, parent and children in both views; editing either view updates both.
close_reason: Backing array drawn under the tree; editing either view edits the same slot; pointing at an index highlights it (blue), its parent (orange) and children (green) in both views; marks shown in both.

title: Heap shape + sketch tool (min/max, complete tree)
description: Heaps are always complete trees: the drag sets n and nodes fill level-order left-to-right as you drag. Random values are heapified (Floyd build-heap); min or max from the style panel; values editable.
acceptance_criteria: Generated heaps satisfy the heap property (vitest); shape is always complete; min/max toggle re-heapifies.
close_reason: Heap shape + tool (Shift+P): drag right inserts one value per cell (fills level order); min/max style with Floyd rebuild; values editable in either view.

title: BST fill and generation modes
description: Any sketched shape becomes a valid BST by giving it sorted distinct random keys in in-order. Generation modes: random insertion order (realistic), balanced (median-first), degenerate (sorted insertion, shows the O(n) worst case).
acceptance_criteria: Every generated/filled tree passes a BST check (vitest); mode selectable in the style panel.
close_reason: BST is a tree kind (drawds:tree-kind): sketched shapes get sorted keys in in-order (always valid; lean = degenerate..balanced); switching a tree to BST keeps its keys and sorts them into place. Tree props migration v2.

title: Wave 5: binary search trees and heaps
description: Ordered trees on top of the binary tree shape: BSTs that are valid by construction, min/max heaps with their backing array, and live invariant checking when values are edited.
notes: Agreed with user (2026-10-02): live operations animate; path highlights fade by default, holding Shift keeps them as marks.
close_reason: Wave 5 core done: BST kind and heaps with animated operations. Invariant checker (dds-55z.18.4) moved to teaching moves.

title: Tree live edits: + on empty child slots, x removes a subtree
description: While a tree is selected and the pointer is near a node: + ghosts on its empty left/right slots add a child there (value per fill mode, opened for editing); x removes the node and its subtree. Tidy layout re-flows after each edit; one undo per edit.
close_reason: Hover a node: + per empty child slot on its lower corners (opens the new child for editing), x removes the subtree (not the root); root stays put; one undo each. e2e.

title: Tree model + tidy layout (Reingold-Tilford / Buchheim)
description: Pure tree model (binary and n-ary) and a tidy layout: parents centred over children, no overlaps, compact; level height and node spacing from the size style; stable (adding a leaf moves few nodes).
acceptance_criteria: vitest covers symmetric, skewed and degenerate trees (no overlaps, parent centred).
close_reason: Contour-based tidy layout for binary trees (lone child offset < half sibling spacing; nulls as phantom leaves); normalised; drag offsets; 16 unit tests incl. no-overlap and parentage clarity.

title: Random binary tree generator (depth + fullness, stable while growing)
description: Generate a random binary tree shape from (depth, fullness 0..1): fullness 1 = complete/perfect, low = sparse and stringy. Growth-stable: increasing depth during a drag only adds the new level, so the tree doesn't reshuffle under the pointer. Seeded.
acceptance_criteria: vitest: deterministic for a seed; depth d+1 contains depth d as a prefix; fullness 1 gives a perfect tree.
close_reason: randomTreePaths(seed, depth, fullness): exact depth via seeded spine, existence by hash(seed, path) so deeper/fuller only adds nodes; ids n+path; random values per perfect-tree index (stable).

title: Wave 4: trees (random binary and n-ary)
description: Sketch a tree in one gesture (tidy layout, random shapes that grow stably as you drag, editable node values). Live moves are part of the wave, not extras: add a child on an empty slot, remove a subtree, show/hide null children, mirror. BSTs and heaps (wave 5) build on this.
close_reason: Wave 4 core done: random binary trees, edits, traversals. n-ary trees (dds-55z.17.4) moved up; mirror (dds-55z.17.6) to teaching moves.

title: Floyd's cycle detection on a circular list (slow / fast)

title: More array algorithms: Hoare partition, merge sort, counting sort
description: Follow-ups to the array algorithms wave. Hoare partition (i and j walking in from both ends, swapping out-of-place pairs; the pivot doesn't necessarily end in place, so narrate that). Merge sort needs an auxiliary array drawn under the original (a strip, or a second row of cells) with values copied down and merged back up. Counting sort needs a counts array. Also consider a playback speed control: bubble sort on 10 values is ~90 steps.
close_reason: Hoare partition (i/j walk in from the off-end slots, swap out-of-place pairs, cross; pivot tracked red; narration notes it isn't necessarily in place), merge sort (call stack + merged strips, taken values fade, copy-back arcs each value into place, comparisons/copies), and the play bar speed control (½x-4x). Counting sort left as dds follow-up.

title: Quicksort partition (Lomuto / Hoare), then quicksort

close_reason: Lomuto partition around the last value (pivot red, smaller values blue, i from lo-1 incl. the -1 slot, j orange, pivot swaps into place green) and full quicksort: range faded outside lo..hi, call stack strip of open calls, emptied at the end. Hoare left for a follow-up.

If ghosts are seen near those, move them into a tldraw overlay layer as the play bar. Frame scenes that reach outside the box (a list node beside the list, reverse's null before the head) and an array step's extra cell (geometry follows it, so that one is fine) remain.

title: Ghost rendering artefacts after pan/zoom on complex drawings
description: Reported 2026-10-02: on busier drawings, after moving and zooming, stale 'ghost' pixels stay on the canvas until something repaints the area (dragging an image over clears them). Not tldraw load (one shape per structure). Likely Chrome paint invalidation missing content we draw outside a shape's geometry bounds: stroke overhang (marked nodes/cells 1.6x), edge-weight pills and BFS/DFS badges near the bounds, the play bar and queue/stack strip, x / + buttons and grow grips, swap-arc animations; CSS fade/slide animations make it likelier. Outside-bounds content can also vanish when tldraw culls a shape at the viewport edge.
design: Fix first: keep every shape's drawing starting at its origin. After edits that change the bounds (remove, add or move a node, connect to empty space, the + grip), shift node positions so the bounds' min corner is (0, 0) and move the shape's x/y by the same amount (rotated), so nothing moves on the page; trees and lists need the same for drag offsets. Do it on drag end rather than mid-drag, so tldraw's handle maths isn't disturbed. Then the earlier items: pad geometry by stroke width and include edge labels and badges; move transient controls (play bar, strip, buttons, grips) into a tldraw overlay layer. Regression check: after deleting the leftmost node, bounds.minX should be 0 and the .tl-shape box should match the drawn extent.
notes:
Related performance item to check in the same QA pass: a selected node-link shape re-renders and re-routes every edge on each pointer move (hover controls read the pointer in component()); memoise routeScene per scene and measure on a 40-node graph.
2026-10-02 screenshot (user's Desktop, 'Screenshot 2026-10-02 at 17.50.45.png'): a directed graph in dark mode; zooming out left copies of the rightmost node's label (12), left behind in stages and bigger the further back, the text only, not the circle. Cause confirmed in the app: tldraw sizes a shape's box from its geometry bounds' width/height but places it at the shape's origin, assuming bounds start at (0, 0). Delete a graph's leftmost nodes and the drawing starts 110 px in (bounds minX 110, width 158): on screen the drawing spans x 386-545 while tldraw's box spans 276-435, so the rightmost node lies outside the box and isn't repainted properly when the camera moves. The same can happen whenever nodes end up left of or above the origin (dragged nodes in graphs, trees and lists, adding a node via the connect or + grips).
close_reason: Fixed in 3b912a5: drawings now start at the shape's origin (layout offset + compensation), so tldraw's box covers them; e2e/bounds.e2e.ts guards it. Leftovers in dds-55z.30.

title: Edge marks for linked lists and trees
description: Graphs mark edges (dds-55z.26.3). Lists (mark a next pointer about to change) and trees (mark a search path's edges) can opt in with markableEdges once their structural edits prune edge marks: list/tree edge keys derive from node ids, so pruneMarks with node ids alone would drop every edge mark.

title: Weighted graph algorithms: Dijkstra, Prim/Kruskal MST; topological sort
description: Step-through on weighted / DAG graphs: tentative distances as node annotations with relaxations animated, MST edges accumulating in green, topological order numbering.
close_reason: src/shapes/graph/algorithms.ts: Dijkstra (distance badges from ∞, best edge into each node green and re-routed on improvement, priority-queue strip, updates count, negative-weight warning, unweighted counts 1), Prim from a node (crossing edges lit, cheapest added, total weight), Kruskal (edges cheapest first strip, cycle-closing edges flashed red, forest when disconnected), topological sort (Kahn: in-degree badges, queue + order strips, placed nodes and removed edges fade, cycle reported, final order numbered). Menu: Dijkstra/Prim on nodes, Graph algorithms submenu (Kruskal undirected, topological sort directed). Strips widen for long items; dim fades edge:<key> too.

title: Heap build-heap (Floyd) step by step (insert and extract are done)
description: Done: insert (sift-up) and remove / extract (sift-down) play step by step with narration in both views. Left: build-heap as an operation: sift down each internal node from the last up, the swaps arcing, with narration; also 'heapify this array' when a heap's values were edited out of order (the invariant checker, dds-55z.18.4, can point at the culprits first).

Heapify-this-array via the invariant checker stays with dds-55z.18.4.

title: BST search walk (insert and delete are done)
description: Done: insert and delete play step by step with narration (comparison path, the three delete cases, successor walk). Left: 'Find a key' from a node's context menu or a prompt: curr walks down comparing (go left / go right), found or falls off at null; pointer curr slides.
close_reason: Search for a node's key or a typed key (BST node context menu, Search submenu): curr walks down from the root narrated as code, each ruled-out subtree fades (new dim support in SceneSvg, edges touching faded nodes fade too), comparisons counter, falls off at null (pointer on the null marker when nulls are shown).

title: Tree traversals: pre/in/post/level order stepping and numbering
description: Teacher moves: 'let's traverse this tree in-order': pick the order and the starting node (any subtree), then walk it step by step: go left / back up / go right, each node numbered as it is visited and its value appended to the output; the recursion shown as the call stack and as the path from the start lit up on the tree; null children as base cases when nulls are shown; level order with its queue. Points made at the end: in-order on a BST gives the keys sorted; level order of a heap is its array order. Built on the play bar (pause, step back, replay).
close_reason: Closed

title: Linked list operations (find, insert, delete, reverse done)
description: Teacher moves on a linked list, step by step on the play bar, with temporary pointers (curr, prev, next) sliding along and every pointer assignment narrated as code: find a value (curr walks, found or null); insert after a node (new node, then node.next = curr.next, then curr.next = node: the order is the lesson); delete a node (prev/curr walk, prev.next = curr.next; head = head.next for the head); reverse (prev/curr/next, arrows flip one by one, head = prev). From a node's context menu. Quick edits (x, + on arrows) stay immediate.

title: Step-through engine: operations as frame sequences
description: Teacher moves while an operation (BST insert/delete, heap insert/extract, BFS/DFS...) runs: pause it mid-way to explain; step forward and back; read a one-line narration per step; run step-by-step from the start in a lecture; finish now or abandon (nothing changes). Frames stay out of undo history until the result commits as one undo step. Built on src/nodelink/playback.ts. Children: play bar + keys, narration, step-by-step mode.
design: Operations are pure generators over the shape model (fits the model-driven representation).
notes: Seeded by src/nodelink/playback.ts (frames, swaps, highlights, commit-at-end). The step-through engine should add pause/step/back on top of it rather than start fresh.
close_reason: Closed
